sentences.text: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Dhar, Judge

Order 
1) The petitioners have challenged the complaint filed by the respondents against them alleging commission of offences under Section 26 (2) (i) & (ii) read with Sections 59 (i) & 51 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 filed before the Court of District Judicial Mobile Magistrate,
Udhampur.

2) It appears that the respondents have filed a complaint against the petitioners before the learned trial Magistrate alleging therein that on 01.08.2019, during routine inspection, the Food Safety Officer inspected the premises of petitioner No. 1/accused at Udhampur.

Sample of wheat (2 kgs.)
was lifted from the premises by the Food Safety Officer and the same was sealed.
The sample was sent for analysis to the Food Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Jammu.

3) As per report of the Food Analyst dated 06.08.2019, it was found that the sample did not conform to the standards prescribed for wheat falling under Regulation No. 2.4.6 (2) of Food Safety Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 with respect to moisture, foreign matters, damaged grains and it contained large number of hairs and rats faecal matter.

entities.text: Food Safety Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Accordingly,
the sample was termed 'unsafe' and 'sub-standard'.
After completing the legal formalities, the impugned complaint came to be filed by the respondents against the petitioners herein.
4) Heard and considered.

1 5)

Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the petitioners are getting the supply of wheat from the Consumer Affairs & Public Distribution Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government for grinding in the mills.

entities.text: Consumer Affairs & Public Distribution Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is submitted that the petitioners do not get the supply of wheat for grinding purpose from any other source.

In this regard, the petitioners have relied upon agreement dated 20th of September 2013 executed between the CAPD Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government and the petitioners, a copy whereof has been placed on record.

entities.text: CAPD Department of Jammu and Kashmir Government
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On this ground, it is urged that if at all the sample was found to be of sub-standard quality, the petitioners cannot be subjected to prosecution and it is the supplier of the wheat, who is to be prosecuted for the said purpose.
6) It is settled law that while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, the High Court cannot go into the defence of the accused.

It is only, if, the accused is able to carve out a case that the contents of the complaint and the material in support thereof, do not constitute an offence against him, that the Court would come to his rescue and quash the criminal proceedings.
7) In the instant case, it is nowhere stated in the complaint that the petitioners were getting the supply of wheat only from the Government.
The allegation against the petitioner is that the sample of wheat lifted from their premises was found to be of sub-standard quality.
The question whether the wheat of which the sample was lifted belonged to the Government or to any other person, would be a subject matter of trial.
The same cannot be gone into by this Court at this stage and in these proceedings.
8) For the foregoing reasons, I do not find any merit in this petition.

The same is, accordingly,
dismissed.
(SANJAY DHAR) JUDGE Jammu 06.03.2023
Karam Chand/Secy.
